// Hand-derived symbols. Anything recovered by fingerprinting against mnsg goes
// in libultra_syms.txt instead, which is generated by
// tools/fingerprint_libultra.py and must not be hand-edited.
//
// Every entry here needs a justification comment: what evidence names it.

// The one function both alSynStopVoice and alSynSetPan call before filling in
// an ALParam, and it sits immediately before __freeParam (0x8002C6D0) in the
// same TU -- the order libultra's synthesizer object has them in. Naming it is
// what let synstopvoice.c and synsetpan.c link.
__allocParam = 0x8002C6A0; // type:func rom:0x2D2A0

// libultra os/exceptasm.s. N64Recomp recognises libultra by name against the
// hardcoded sets in its src/symbol_lists.cpp; every name below is in its
// ignored_funcs, so naming them is all that is needed -- none has to be
// decompiled. Left under func_XXXXXXXX placeholders they get recompiled as game
// code and choke on the cop0 accesses.
//
// splat found only three functions in this run of code (0x800270B0, 0x800275E4,
// 0x80027824), because the rest are reached by branch rather than jal. The
// entries below restore the real seven, and the identification is the
// instruction sequence of each -- exceptasm.s is handwritten and unchanged
// between libultra 2.0H games, so each one is recognisable on sight:

// lui/addiu/jr $k0 into 0x800270C0 and nothing else. The trampoline the
// exception vector at 0x80000180 is filled with.
__osExceptionPreamble = 0x800270B0; // type:func rom:0x27CB0

// The target of that jr, and the exception handler proper: saves $at through
// $ra into __osThreadSave, reads cop0 Cause (13) and Status (12), and dispatches
// on the ExcCode. splat had folded it into __osExceptionPreamble.
__osException = 0x800270C0; // type:func rom:0x27CC0

// exceptasm.s's internal `jal send_mesg` helper -- __osException calls it with
// $a0 = the byte offset of an entry in __osEventStateTab (0x800CD5F0), and it
// appends the entry's message to that event's queue, then unblocks a waiter via
// __osPopThread/__osEnqueueThread. It saves $ra in $s2 and returns `jr $s2`,
// which is why it is not a normal leaf.
send_mesg = 0x800275E4; // type:func rom:0x281E4

// The coprocessor-unusable handler, which splat had folded into the tail of
// send_mesg -- hence "branches outside itself". It masks Cause with 0x30000000,
// shifts the CE field down by 28, and takes the path for coprocessor 1: set
// SR_CU1 (0x20000000) in the saved Status word and mark the thread FP-using.
handle_CpU = 0x80027698; // type:func rom:0x28298

// Restores a thread's full register context from __osRunningThread and ends in
// `mtc0 $k1, $14` (EPC) followed by eret. It is the only function in the ROM
// that writes EPC, which is what identifies it.
__osDispatchThread = 0x80027824; // type:func rom:0x28424

// `jal osDestroyThread` with $a0 = 0 and no return -- the two instructions every
// thread's $ra is seeded with. splat had it inside __osDispatchThread, reached
// only by falling off the eret.
__osCleanupThread = 0x800279A0; // type:func rom:0x285A0

// libultra os/getcause.s, in full: `mfc0 $v0, $13` / `jr $ra` / `nop`. A
// three-instruction leaf that reads cop0 Cause and returns it can be nothing
// else.
__osGetCause = 0x80033E00; // type:func rom:0x34A00

// Eight jal targets in .file_7, the permanently resident overlay at 0x80107830,
// that splat could not attribute to a segment because the caller lives in
// .main. It emitted them into .splat/usa/undefined_funcs_auto.ld as absolute
// symbols (`func_80126744 = 0x80126744;`), which links fine but erases the
// section, and N64Recomp needs the section to resolve a cross-section call.
// Asserting the name here is what makes splat emit the real, section-bearing
// symbol instead.
//
// The evidence for each is that splat itself already names a FUNC at exactly
// that vram inside .file_7 -- these only restate what the overlay's own
// disassembly says, and every one is unambiguous: .file_7 is the sole tenant of
// its RAM slot, so no other overlay defines a function at the same address.
//
// This is the complete set. tools/undefined_funcs_report.py checks every entry
// in undefined_funcs_auto.ld against the ELF's section layout and reports the
// ones whose callers sit outside the target's section; only these eight, plus
// the two rspboot pseudo-functions the recompiler ignores, ever crossed.
// Callers: func_80001454_2054, func_800021B4_2DB4, func_800183D0_18FD0.
func_80126744_505E54 = 0x80126744; // type:func rom:0x505E54
func_80133AA0_5131B0 = 0x80133AA0; // type:func rom:0x5131B0
func_80141108_520818 = 0x80141108; // type:func rom:0x520818
func_801414B0_520BC0 = 0x801414B0; // type:func rom:0x520BC0
func_80141934_521044 = 0x80141934; // type:func rom:0x521044
func_80151BFC_53130C = 0x80151BFC; // type:func rom:0x53130C
func_80151DA4_5314B4 = 0x80151DA4; // type:func rom:0x5314B4
func_801521C8_5318D8 = 0x801521C8; // type:func rom:0x5318D8

// The fourth has no symbol: splat merged two adjacent 8-byte stubs into one
// 0x10-byte func_80152230_531940, because nothing reachable named the second.
// The bytes are `jr $ra / nop / jr $ra / nop` -- two independent do-nothing
// functions, not one function with an alternate entry point. func_801BF248 in
// .file_23 jals the second at 0x80152238, so it needs its own symbol.
func_80152238_531948 = 0x80152238; // type:func rom:0x531948 size:0x8

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// libultra functions that Phase D found blocking, by compiling the recompiled
// output for the first time.
//
// N64Recomp does not recompile a function named in its ignored_funcs or
// reimplemented_funcs lists; where one is *called* it emits <name>_recomp and
// expects N64ModernRuntime to define it. While these sat under placeholders the
// recompiler emitted the game's OWN copies, which both failed to compile (they
// call named internals with no host implementation) and would have run the
// game's SI/VI/PI drivers against registers librecomp does not emulate.
//
// mnsg could not supply these by fingerprinting: it lacks osStopThread
// altogether, and its osInitialize, osCreateViManager and osPfsInitPak differ
// in size from Hybrid Heaven's, so the library builds are not identical here.
// Each is identified from its own instructions instead.
//
// HybridHeaven-Recomp/tools/recomp_symbol_gap.py is the check. It should reach
// zero; __osContRamRead and __osContRamWrite are deliberately still unnamed,
// because ~14 unnamed osPfs functions call them and naming them alone would
// move the gap rather than close it.

// Installs the exception handler by copying __osExceptionPreamble, reads the
// IPL3 globals at 0x80000300 (osTvType), sets cop0 SR, and maps the rdb TLB
// entry. The only function that touches all of __osSetSR, osMapTLBRdb,
// osUnmapTLBAll and __osExceptionPreamble. Called from the boot function
// func_80001078_1C78, which the entry stub jumps to.
osInitialize = 0x80028B10; // type:func rom:0x29710

// The SI raw IO pair, called only by osInitialize. Both check __osSiDeviceBusy
// and return -1 if busy; the read loads from (devAddr | 0xA0000000) into *data,
// the write stores data to it. That direction is the whole difference.
__osSiRawReadIo = 0x80029640;  // type:func rom:0x2A240
__osSiRawWriteIo = 0x80034640; // type:func rom:0x35240

// Checks __osSpDeviceBusy, writes devAddr to SP_MEM_ADDR (0xA4040000) and
// osVirtualToPhysical(dramAddr) to SP_DRAM_ADDR (0xA4040004), then size-1 to
// SP_RD_LEN (0xA4040008) or SP_WR_LEN (0xA404000C) depending on direction.
// Nothing calls it in this ROM.
__osSpRawStartDma = 0x80029440; // type:func rom:0x2A040

// Takes the saved interrupt mask from __osDisableInt, then switches on the
// thread state at +0x10: RUNNING (4, which is also the state assumed when the
// argument is NULL) sets __osRunningThread's state to STOPPED (1) and calls
// __osEnqueueAndYield(NULL); RUNNABLE (2) and WAITING (8) set the thread's own
// state to STOPPED and call __osDequeueThread(thread->queue, thread).
osStopThread = 0x800265F0; // type:func rom:0x271F0

// __osSiGetAccess, then -- only if __osContLastCmd != 1 -- pack, write-DMA and
// wait, then read-DMA and store 1 back to __osContLastCmd. The constant is
// CONT_CMD_READ_BUTTON (1), and the packer is called with no argument, which is
// what separates this from osContStartQuery: that one uses
// CONT_CMD_REQUEST_STATUS (0) and passes it to __osPackRequestData.
osContStartReadData = 0x800283B0; // type:func rom:0x28FB0

// Returns PFS_ERR_INVALID (5) unless pfs->status has PFS_MOTOR_INITIALIZED (8),
// then fills a 64-byte per-channel block with the flag argument, sets the pif
// status word and __osContLastCmd = CONT_CMD_END (0xFE), and runs a
// write-DMA/recv/read-DMA/recv cycle. osMotorStart and osMotorStop are macros
// over this in 2.0H, which is why game code calls it directly from two sites.
__osMotorAccess = 0x80027A90; // type:func rom:0x28690

// Manager pairs: each creates its message queues, reads and raises its thread
// priority, creates and starts a thread, and the thread's entry point is the
// second function of the pair. Neither entry point is ever `jal`ed -- they are
// only taken as addresses -- which is why each has no callers at all.
//
// The VI pair calls __osViInit; its thread proc calls __osViGetCurrentContext
// and __osTimerInterrupt and drives the retrace messages.
osCreateViManager = 0x800346C0; // type:func rom:0x352C0
viMgrMain = 0x80034840;         // type:func rom:0x35440

// The PI pair calls __osPiCreateAccessQueue; its thread proc is the device
// manager loop -- a jump-table dispatch over PI_STATUS_REG (0xA4600010) wrapped
// in __osSetGlobalIntMask / __osResetGlobalIntMask.
osCreatePiManager = 0x8002AC60; // type:func rom:0x2B860
__osDevMgrMain = 0x8002AEA0;    // type:func rom:0x2BAA0

// __osSiGetAccess, __osPfsGetStatus(queue, channel), __osSiRelAccess, and on
// success stores queue at pfs+4, channel at pfs+8 and zeroes pfs->status --
// the signature osPfsInitPak(OSMesgQueue *, OSPfs *, int) exactly.
osPfsInitPak = 0x80032FB0; // type:func rom:0x33BB0

// Found by actually running the port: the first thing the recompiled game did
// after osInitialize was fault here, inside the boot function
// func_80001078_1C78.
//
// It walks a candidate size from 0x400000 up in 0x100000 steps while it is
// below 0x800000, and at each step writes an inverted word through KSEG1
// (0xA0000000) and reads it back to see whether memory aliases, returning the
// size in $v0. That is osGetMemSize and nothing else -- and it is precisely the
// failure this repo's placeholders cause: unnamed, it was recompiled and run,
// and librecomp maps KSEG0 only, so the uncached probe walked ~0.5GB past the
// end of rdram and into the guard page.
//
// Named, it is both `ignored` and `reimplemented` in N64Recomp, and librecomp
// answers with the 8MB it configures in recomp::init. mnsg has no osGetMemSize
// at all, which is why fingerprinting never offered it.
osGetMemSize = 0x8002C0B0; // type:func rom:0x2CCB0

// The second runtime crash, from game code via func_80001E70_2A70. It takes the
// PI access mutex, zeroes a 0x60-byte handle, sets its baseAddress to
// 0xB0000000 (the cart domain) and fills the rest from the PI BSD domain
// registers at 0xA4600014-0xA4600020. That is osCartRomInit, and librecomp
// reimplements it -- its pi.cpp does the same `handle->baseAddress =
// phys_to_k1(recomp::rom_base)`.
//
// Note what is NOT named alongside it. Four more unnamed libultra functions
// touch PI registers -- func_8002B2B0_2BEB0, func_80030C60_31860,
// func_80030E10_31A10 and func_80034400_35000, the raw DMA and raw IO
// primitives. Every one of them is in N64Recomp's ignored_funcs but has NO host
// implementation, so naming them would re-open the symbol gap. They are also
// dead: the only things that reach them are osCreatePiManager (which takes two
// of their addresses for the device manager's dma/edma pointers) and
// __osDevMgrMain, and both of those are now named, so librecomp's versions run
// instead and the game's copies are never entered.
//
// The rule this follows: name a libultra function when the runtime provides it,
// not merely because the recompiler would skip it.
osCartRomInit = 0x80032BE0; // type:func rom:0x337E0

// The third runtime crash, from func_800011B0_1DB0. Between __osDisableInt and
// __osRestoreInt it walks the low bits of its argument in on/off pairs -- bit 0
// sets 0x8 in __osViNext->features, bit 1 clears it, bit 2 sets 0x4, and so on.
// That structure is osViSetSpecialFeatures and its OS_VI_GAMMA_ON /
// OS_VI_GAMMA_OFF style flag pairs; Quest64-Decomp's call graph for it
// (__osDisableInt, __osError, __osRestoreInt) agrees.
//
// It faulted because __osViNext (D_8004AED4) is the game's own copy of VI state
// and nothing initialises it any more -- osCreateViManager is named, so
// librecomp's version runs and owns the VI context. Reading through the null
// pointer walked off rdram. Naming it hands the call to the runtime, which is
// where the real VI state lives.
osViSetSpecialFeatures = 0x80032890; // type:func rom:0x33490

// The first runtime HANG rather than crash, and the one that kept the overlay
// loader from ever completing a load. The game's DMA wrapper func_80001F30_2B30
// fills an OSIoMesg, calls this, then blocks in osRecvMesg waiting for the
// completion message. Unnamed, this ran the game's own copy, which only queues
// the request onto a PI command queue that librecomp's native PI manager does
// not service -- so the completion never arrived and the boot thread waited
// forever.
//
// It is osEPiStartDma, matched instruction for instruction against libultra:
// returns -1 unless __osPiDevMgr.active (D_8004AB10_4B710) is set; stores the
// handle at mb->piHandle (offset 0x14); sets mb->hdr.type to 0xF
// OS_MESG_TYPE_DMAREAD or 0x10 OS_MESG_TYPE_DMAWRITE by direction; then jams or
// sends the message NOBLOCK depending on whether mb->hdr.pri (offset 0x2) is 1
// OS_MESG_PRI_HIGH. Its three arguments (pihandle, mb, direction) match the
// prototype exactly, and the already-named osPiStartDma next door in
// main_2CBA0.s has the same shape with the extra fields filled in.
//
// The runtime provides it -- librecomp's pi.cpp defines osEPiStartDma_recomp --
// which is the test that naming helps, not merely that the recompiler skips it.
//
// Naming this also kills func_800326F0_332F0 (osPiGetCmdQueue), whose only two
// callers are this function and osPiStartDma; both are native afterwards. That
// one is deliberately NOT named: the runtime has no osPiGetCmdQueue_recomp, so
// naming it would re-open the symbol gap for no gain.
osEPiStartDma = 0x800304F0; // type:func rom:0x310F0

// The crash after the DMA fix, and the reason it was a crash inside the runtime
// rather than in game code. func_800021B4_2DB4 reads the controller:
// osContStartReadData, then osRecvMesg on D_8005CE20_5DA20, then unpack. But
// ultramodern's osContStartReadData IGNORES its queue argument and posts to
// events_context.si.mq (ultramodern::send_si_message), and the only thing that
// ever sets that is osSetEventMesg(OS_EVENT_SI, ...). Its osContInit does not.
// So si.mq stayed null and do_send dereferenced it -- the segfault landed in
// ultramodern/src/mesgqueue.cpp, one frame below osRecvMesg_recomp.
//
// This is osSetEventMesg. It calls __osDisableInt, indexes D_800CD5F0_CE1F0 by
// (event << 3) -- that address is already identified as __osEventStateTab by
// send_mesg in exceptasm.s, which is independent corroboration -- stores the
// queue at +0x0 and the message at +0x4, then special-cases event 0xE
// (OS_EVENT_PRENMI) by sending the message immediately with OS_MESG_NOBLOCK,
// and finishes with __osRestoreInt. Its call site is the giveaway too: the boot
// path calls osCreateMesgQueue, then this, then osContInit, on the same queue.
//
// librecomp defines osSetEventMesg_recomp in ultra_translation.cpp.
osSetEventMesg = 0x8002FB60; // type:func rom:0x30760

// Called immediately after that osRecvMesg, on D_8005CE50_5DA50. It loops over
// a count at D_800CBFC1_CCBC1, copying 8-byte records out of the SI response
// buffer at D_800CBF80_CCB80 with unaligned lwl/lwr pairs and unpacking them
// into OSContPad-shaped output. That is osContGetReadData, which librecomp
// provides in cont.cpp -- and it has to be native, because the buffer it would
// otherwise read is the game's own SI DMA destination, which nothing fills now
// that osContStartReadData is the runtime's.
osContGetReadData = 0x80028434; // type:func rom:0x29034

// Handwritten cop0 code from os/setintmask.s: mfc0 $t0, $12 (Status), clear the
// IE bit with and $t1, $t0, -2, mtc0 it back, and return the old IE bit in $v0.
// The tail reconciles the thread's status word against __osGlobalIntMask
// (D_80049980_4A580) the way libultra 2.0H's version does. __osRestoreInt, its
// counterpart, is already named, which is what makes the pairing legible.
//
// Naming it matters for the same reason exceptasm.s did in Phase C: these are
// privileged instructions the recompiler should never have to translate.
// librecomp defines __osDisableInt_recomp in ultra_translation.cpp.
__osDisableInt = 0x80032660; // type:func rom:0x33260

// The crash once boot reached audio init, and the first one raised from inside a
// loaded overlay: the call chain runs func_80005270_5E70 -> func_80107830_4E6F40
// (code in .file_7, so the loader hook had already registered it) ->
// func_800201D0_20DD0 -> func_8001F8A0_204A0 -> here.
//
// This is osAiSetFrequency. It converts its u32 argument to float, divides
// D_80049978_4A578 (osViClock) by it, adds 0.5f to round, and then writes the
// result to D_A4500010 and D_A4500014 -- AI_DACRATE_REG and AI_BITRATE_REG. The
// cfc1/ctc1 dance around cvt.w.s is IDO's standard float-to-unsigned sequence,
// and osViClock as the numerator is what fixes the identity: no other libultra
// function divides the video clock to program the audio DAC.
//
// It faulted for the same reason osGetMemSize did -- those are KSEG1 addresses
// (0xA4500010), and librecomp maps KSEG0 only, so the store walked off rdram.
// librecomp provides osAiSetFrequency_recomp in ai.cpp, and its siblings
// osAiGetLength and osAiSetNextBuffer are already named here, so this was the
// last unnamed function in the AI family.
//
// It is also the last unnamed libultra function called from game code that
// touches hardware registers at all; the rest of that list is computation or
// runtime-owned state.
osAiSetFrequency = 0x80031670; // type:func rom:0x32270

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The osPfs subsystem, named as a unit.
//
// This is the closure the port has been stopping in. __osSiGetAccess and
// __osSiRelAccess are deliberately stubbed to abort in
// HybridHeaven-Recomp/src/game/ultra_missing.cpp, because librecomp reimplements
// the twelve public osPfs entry points in pak.cpp and provides NO SI-level
// support at all -- so everything beneath the public API is meant never to run.
// Naming a subset only moves the boundary, which is why these go in together.
//
// The closure was computed rather than guessed: walking the call graph upward
// from the two functions that actually reach the SI stubs
// (func_80034060_34C60 = __osContRamRead, func_80033E10_34A10 = __osContRamWrite)
// gives exactly 23 unnamed libultra functions, which is the number this repo's
// notes have carried since Phase D. Of those 23, exactly ten have callers in
// game code, and librecomp provides exactly ten public osPfs entry points that
// are not already named here (osPfsInitPak and osPfsIsPlug were named earlier).
// That one-to-one fit is itself part of the evidence.
//
// Everything below the public API stays unnamed on purpose -- __osContRamRead,
// __osContRamWrite, __osPfsSelectBank, __osPfsRWInode and the rest have no
// host implementation, so naming them would re-open the symbol gap. Once these
// eleven are named nothing reaches them, and the SI stubs stay as a tripwire.
//
// Identified from argument signatures and call graphs, corroborated against
// Quest64-Decomp's src/libultra/io/pfs*.c call graphs (its bytes do not match --
// the best structural score across the 23 was 0.24 -- but its call graphs do).

// 7 args, and `andi $t6, $a1, 0xFFFF` types a1 as the u16 company_code. The
// only public entry point that calls two others: osPfsFindFile (0x8002EE40)
// and osPfsFreeBlocks (0x80026450), exactly as pfsallocatefile.c does.
osPfsAllocateFile = 0x8002A350; // type:func rom:0x2AF50

// One argument, a 0x4C8 stack frame for its working buffers, and 334
// instructions -- the largest in the closure. Its only caller is osPfsInitPak,
// and Quest64's pfsinitPFSPaks.c confirms osPfsInitPak calls osPfsChecker.
osPfsChecker = 0x800332C0; // type:func rom:0x33EC0

// 5 args -- a1 is again a u16 company_code, and the fifth is read from
// 0x180($sp) past a 0x170 frame. Calls osPfsFindFile, as pfsdeletefile.c does.
osPfsDeleteFile = 0x80031BC0; // type:func rom:0x327C0

// 3 args, and a1 is a file number: it is bounds-checked against pfs->0x50 (the
// directory size) with `slt` before use, then rejected if negative.
osPfsFileState = 0x80032DD0; // type:func rom:0x339D0

// The one public function called by BOTH osPfsAllocateFile and osPfsDeleteFile,
// which in libultra is only true of osPfsFindFile.
osPfsFindFile = 0x8002EE40; // type:func rom:0x2FA40

// 2 args -- only a0 (pfs, whose status word it loads first) and a1, an out
// pointer. Called by osPfsAllocateFile, as pfsallocatefile.c does.
osPfsFreeBlocks = 0x80026450; // type:func rom:0x27050

// This name is WRONG and is kept deliberately. Read the rest of this comment
// before "fixing" it, and read func_80002A94_3694 before renaming it.
//
// It stores a0 into pfs->0x4 (the message queue), a2 into pfs->0x8 (the channel),
// clears pfs->0x0 (status) and sets pfs->0x65 (activebank) to 0xFF -- so far, the
// shape of any osPfs/osMotor initialiser. What it does next is not osPfsInit's:
//
//   __osPfsSelectBank(pfs, 0xFE); __osContRamRead(CONT_BLOCK_DETECT);
//   if (block[31] == 0xFE) return PFS_ERR_DEVICE;
//   __osPfsSelectBank(pfs, 0x80); __osContRamRead(CONT_BLOCK_DETECT);
//   if (block[31] != 0x80) return PFS_ERR_DEVICE;
//
// Two bank probes and two PFS_ERR_DEVICE returns: a device-identification probe
// for a pak that answers 0x80. libultra's osPfsInit selects bank 0 and checksums
// the ID area, and never touches bank 0xFE. The game agrees with this reading --
// func_80002A94_3694 calls this function and, on success, sets the RUMBLE-available
// flag D_80037780_38380, which gates __osMotorAccess(pfs, 1).
//
// (0x80031FF0 is genuinely osMotorInit: it __osContRamWRITEs a block of 0xFE, then
// one of 0x84. Writing the detect block is what separates the two.)
//
// The name stays because it is what makes the port work. N64Recomp routes this
// call to librecomp's osPfsInit_recomp, which returns PFS_OK, which is what keeps
// the rumble alive; there is no better target, since librecomp implements no
// osGbpakInit. The save path's dependence on this function was removed on the
// game's side instead -- HybridHeaven-Recomp/patches/pak.c.
osPfsInit = 0x80027D04; // type:func rom:0x28904

// 3 args, and it writes through BOTH pointer arguments near the end --
// `sw $s2, 0x0($t5)` and `sw $t6, 0x0($t7)` from the saved a2 and a1. That
// two-out-pointer shape is osPfsNumFiles(pfs, *max_files, *files_used).
osPfsNumFiles = 0x80032AB0; // type:func rom:0x336B0

// 6 args, and the types settle it: a1 is a file number bounds-checked against
// pfs->0x50, `andi $s0, $a2, 0xFF` makes a2 the u8 read/write flag, a3 is the
// offset, and the remaining two are read from 0x180/0x184($sp) past a 0x170
// frame. 222 instructions, the largest of the game-called ten.
osPfsReadWriteFile = 0x80029784; // type:func rom:0x2A384

// 22 instructions, one argument. Tests pfs->status against 0x5
// (PFS_INITIALIZED | PFS_ID_BROKEN), calls the repair helper, and on success
// clears bit 0x4 with `and $t9, $t8, -0x5`. Clearing PFS_ID_BROKEN is what
// osPfsRepairId is for.
osPfsRepairId = 0x800308D0; // type:func rom:0x314D0

// Not osPfs, but in the same closure and found by the same walk. 3 args, clears
// pfs->status through a1, and fills a 32-byte stack buffer with 0xFE before
// writing it to the pak -- libultra's osMotorInit block-detect probe, which
// writes BLOCKSIZE bytes of 254. librecomp provides osMotorInit_recomp.
osMotorInit = 0x80031FF0; // type:func rom:0x32BF0

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Two functions in .file_56 that splat ends early, which silently truncates a
// jump table in the recompiled port.
//
// splat ends a function at a `jr $ra` and opens a new symbol on the next
// instruction. Here that next instruction is a jump-table CASE BODY, not a new
// function -- both spurious symbols have zero jal callers, while every genuine
// neighbour (0x8035A434, 0x8035AA44) has them. The size is what makes it a bug
// rather than a cosmetic split: N64Recomp's analysis.cpp sizes a jump table by
// walking entries while they fall inside [func.vram, func.vram + size), so a
// short size drops every case at or past the boundary and the recompiled switch
// gets a switch_error default for indices the game bounds-checks as legal.
// librecomp's switch_error calls exit() from a game thread, which is a crash.
//
// The evidence for each is the game's own bounds check versus the table.

// `sltiu $at, $a0, 0x8` -- an 8-entry table at 0x8038A000. Entry 2 is
// 0x8035A428, exactly the exclusive end of the declared 0x50, so the table was
// cut to 2 entries and a0 in 2..7 aborted. Absorbs func_8035A428_7FE048 (0xC),
// whose three instructions (`or $v0,$zero,$zero / jr $ra / nop`) are the
// return-0 case. Ends at 0x8035A434, which has two jal callers.
func_8035A3D8_7FDFF8 = 0x8035A3D8; // type:func rom:0x7FDFF8 size:0x5C

// `sltiu $at, $a0, 0x5` -- a 5-entry table at 0x8038A020, terminated in the ROM
// by the float 0x3DCCCCCD. Entry 3 is 0x8035A9E0, the exclusive end of the
// declared 0xA8, so it was cut to 3. Absorbs BOTH func_8035A9E0_7FE600 (0x34)
// and func_8035AA14_7FE634 (0x30) -- the latter is entry 4, so stopping after
// the first would still leave the last case unreachable. Ends at 0x8035AA44.
func_8035A938_7FE558 = 0x8035A938; // type:func rom:0x7FE558 size:0x10C
